title: Lottery Tax by State: Exact Take-Home Amounts (2026)
description: Win a $200M Powerball jackpot? See exactly what you keep after federal and state taxes — from $62.4M in Florida to $55.9M in New York.
content:
What This Article Calculates and Why Your State Changes Everything

If you won $200 million in Powerball tonight — say the jackpot had been live on the November 4, 2026 draw (winning numbers: 15, 34, 41, 53, 56 + PB 21) — your first question would not be "how do I celebrate?" It would be "how much do I actually keep?" The answer depends almost entirely on where you live. Use our lottery tax calculator to run your own numbers instantly, or read through this complete breakdown to understand exactly how lottery tax by state works from first principles.

The difference between winning in a no-tax state like Florida versus a high-tax state like New York is not a rounding error. On a $200 million jackpot, that difference exceeds $6.5 million in cash you either keep or surrender. This article shows you the exact dollar figures at every step — lump sum cash value, federal withholding, top marginal federal rate, and each state's specific bite — so you know precisely what check you would deposit.

The Baseline Jackpot: How We Run the Numbers on a $200M Powerball Win

Every calculation in this article starts from the same point: a $200,000,000 advertised Powerball jackpot. That headline number is the annuity value — what you receive if you take 30 annual payments over 29 years. Most winners take the lump sum cash option instead.

The Lump Sum Reduction

The lump sum cash value is typically 60% of the advertised jackpot. On a $200 million jackpot, that equals $120,000,000 before any taxes. That is the number the IRS and your state revenue department see on day one.

Note: The exact cash value varies slightly by jackpot and draw date. Powerball publishes the specific cash option amount alongside each jackpot. We use the standard 60% figure here for consistent comparison across all states.

Federal Tax Calculation: What the IRS Takes First

Federal taxes apply to every winner in every state. There is no avoiding them. Here is exactly what happens to your $120,000,000 lump sum at the federal level.

Step 1: Mandatory Federal Withholding

The IRS requires Powerball to withhold 24% of any prize over $5,000 immediately at the time of payment. On $120,000,000, that withholding equals $28,800,000. You receive a check for $91,200,000 after withholding, but that is not your final tax bill — it is a down payment.

Step 2: Top Marginal Rate at Tax Filing

A $120,000,000 windfall pushes every dollar of your winnings far above the top federal marginal bracket. For single filers in 2026, the 37% rate applies to income above $626,350. Effectively, your entire jackpot lump sum is taxed at 37%. Total federal tax owed: $44,400,000. Since withholding already covered $28,800,000, you owe an additional $15,600,000 when you file your return.

Federal Take-Home After Full 37% Rate

Subtract the full $44,400,000 in federal taxes from your $120,000,000 lump sum. You are left with $75,600,000 before state taxes. That is your starting point for every state calculation below.

Lump Sum vs. Annuity: Exact Dollar Difference on a $200M Win

Every winner faces this choice: take $120,000,000 today (lump sum) or receive 30 graduated payments totaling $200,000,000 (annuity). Here are the exact dollar implications of each path on a $200 million jackpot, assuming a no-state-tax state like Florida.

OptionPre-Tax AmountFederal Tax (37%)State Tax (FL: 0%)Final Take-Home
Lump Sum$120,000,000$44,400,000$0$75,600,000
Annuity (30 payments)$200,000,000~$74,000,000$0~$126,000,000

Annuity federal tax is estimated at 37% applied to each annual payment. Actual annuity payments increase by approximately 5% per year. Final annuity net is an approximation across the full 29-year payment schedule.

The annuity delivers roughly $50,400,000 more in total after-tax dollars than the lump sum — but spread over three decades. Whether that trade-off makes sense depends on your personal financial situation, investment capacity, and life expectancy. For this article, all state comparisons use the lump sum since that is the choice the majority of jackpot winners make.

The difference between winning in New York versus Florida on a $200M Powerball jackpot lump sum is $6,513,000 in cash — money that goes to the state government instead of your bank account.

How to Calculate Your Own Lottery Tax Liability

You do not need to guess at your own numbers. Here is the exact four-step process to calculate what you would keep from any jackpot in any state. For instant results, use our lottery tax calculator, which applies current federal and state rates automatically.

  1. Find the lump sum cash value. Multiply the advertised jackpot by 60%. Example: $200M × 0.60 = $120,000,000.
  2. Apply the full federal rate. Multiply the lump sum by 37% to find your total federal tax. Example: $120,000,000 × 0.37 = $44,400,000. Subtract from the lump sum: $120,000,000 − $44,400,000 = $75,600,000.
  3. Apply your state's income tax rate to the gross lump sum. Do not apply state tax to the post-federal amount — most states tax the full prize amount. Example for Minnesota: $120,000,000 × 0.0985 = $11,820,000 in state tax.
  4. Subtract state tax from your federal after-tax amount. Example for Minnesota: $75,600,000 − $11,820,000 = $63,780,000.

If you live in a city with a local income tax — most notably New York City — add a fifth step: apply the local rate to the gross lump sum and subtract that additional amount. NYC's top local rate of 3.876% costs a New York City resident an additional $4,651,200 on a $120,000,000 lump sum, reducing total take-home to approximately $57,868,800.

These calculations assume single-filer status and no deductions or credits that could offset the tax liability. Your actual tax situation may differ. A qualified tax professional or CPA specializing in lottery winnings can account for your specific filing status, existing income, and available deductions.
